messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Multiple 401/500s for tenant 'kaldera-prod' (Private VPC). Trigger: auth-introspect error rate spike > threshold. Paging eng-sre and devops. thread_ts=3897654321

maya: I'm taking first touch. Seeing alerts for identity-proxy (ip-identity-01) in kaldera VPC. Error pattern: jwks fetch 5xx -> token introspection fails -> downstream 401s.

chris: I'm in. Can you paste the recent identity-proxy logs?

maya: gist of logs below (redacted):

``` 
2026-03-15T10:02:18Z ip-identity-01 ERROR fetch_jwks failed status=502 url=https://auth-keys.kaldera.internal/.well-known/jwks.json err=upstream_timeout
2026-03-15T10:02:19Z ip-identity-01 WARN no_kid_match for token kid=abc123
2026-03-15T10:02:20Z ip-identity-01 ERROR introspect failed status=500 err=key_lookup_failed
```

maya: Also seeing our jwks-cache miss rate spike, cache refresh jobs backoff.

chris: Running curl from a bastion in the same VPC to auth-keys:``` 
curl -v https://auth-keys.kaldera.internal/.well-known/jwks.json --resolve auth-keys.kaldera.internal:443:10.12.45.23
# HTTP/1.1 503 Service Temporarily Unavailable
```

sam-solutions: Kaldera reports 100% of API calls failing for their web app. They're on a live demo today. Customer is already on the call. cc @customer-kaldera

customer-kaldera: Confirming, web UI completely broken for some users. Using their SSO stack. Please advise ETA.

maya: Immediate mitigation plan options: 1) point identity-proxy to the long-lived cached JWKS snapshot we keep in S3 (fast). 2) Roll back the customer's latest JWKS rotation (if they performed one) via our tenant bridge. 3) Enable a temporary permissive fallback (accept tokens with matching alg only) - risky. Thoughts?

chris: Let's do (1) first — minimal blast radius. I can flip identity-proxy config to load jwks from S3 snapshot and bypass live fetch. Doing it on ip-identity-01 group now.

devops-jen: I can push the config change via Ansible. Command I'm about to run (dry-run then apply):
```
ansible-playbook playbooks/identity-proxy/enable-jwks-snapshot.yml --extra-vars "env=kaldera-prod target=ip-identity-01"
```

deploy-bot: :gear: deploy started by devops-jen on ip-identity-01 (run id: d-20260315-007).

maya: Applied on primary pool. Observability: jwks fetch attempts stopped, cache used. Error rate dropping.

chris: Confirming token introspection success on a few requests now: 200/200 for saml/oidc tokens. Latency looks normal.

customer-kaldera: We're seeing partial recovery, thanks. Some older sessions still 401ing. We're doing refresh.

maya: Implemented additional fallback on identity-proxy to accept tokens signed by the previous KID for 1 hour while we validate the customer's rotation artifact.

sam-solutions: Customer IT says they rotated their keys ~09:58 UTC using an internal job; our bridge attempted to fetch new jwks but their internal key server returned 503 and then started returning a malformed JSON for ~30s which triggered our cache eviction job.

chris: Root cause hypothesis: customer rotated keys, upstream key server experienced a transient failure/malformed payload causing our jwks-fetch to treat response as authoritative empty set -> cache cleared -> introspection fails.

maya: Next steps: 1) Keep S3 snapshot fallback active for 45m. 2) Coordinate with Kaldera to re-publish a correct jwks blob. 3) After customer confirms valid jwks, run a controlled resume of live fetch with increased validation and not evicting on single malformed response. 4) Post-incident follow-up: add circuit-breaker to avoid cache eviction on 5xx/malformed.

devops-jen: Patch to identity-proxy ready, will add strict JSON schema validation and treat malformed as transient (log+metric, no eviction). PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/identity-proxy/pulls/431 (ops-testing).

sre-lead: Good mitigation. Assigning oncall follow-up tasks: maya (primary), chris (verification), devops-jen (patch backport & canary), sam-solutions (customer liaison).

maya: Handoff to chris in 20m for monitoring window. If error rate stays <1% for 20m we close page; else escalate to db/infra.

chris: Monitoring window started 10:18 UTC. Keeping an eye on token-introspect error rate and jwks-cache-miss.

customer-kaldera: We've re-published a corrected jwks.json and it's available at their internal endpoint. We'll provide the SHA256 and an example curl to validate.

customer-kaldera: sha256=af3b1f... ; curl shows valid JSON and keys present.

devops-jen: Performing controlled resume: switching identity-proxy to fetch mode but with defensive flags (validate-json=true, ignore-on-malformed=true, min-cache-ttl=60s). Applying to canary pool ip-identity-02.

deploy-bot: :gear: canary deploy started (d-20260315-008) to ip-identity-02.

chris: Canary successful, canary logs show no eviction on a transient malformed response. Introspects continue to succeed. Scaling config to full pool in 5m.

maya: Rolling to full pool now. Watching metrics.

chris: All green. Error rate back to baseline. Kaldera confirms full recovery at 10:34 UTC.

customer-kaldera: Confirmed — production traffic healthy. Thank you team for quick mitigation and clear comms.

maya: Closing the page. Next: file a postmortem with timeline, mitigations, and a checklist for customer-triggered rotations. Action items assigned in follow-up.

sre-lead: Please include the suggested product change: do not evict JWKS cache on single fetch failure; add a schema validation gate; alert on malformed jwks with severity.

chris: Noted. I'll start the post-incident doc and include logs.

maya: Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
